metadata.summary: Background: The molecular mechanisms underlying heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) (HF-MI) remain incompletely understood, and whole-transcriptome profiling studies hold significant promise for disease prevention and treatment. Methods: Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on post-MI patients with and without HF to analyze differentially expressed mRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, along with functional enrichment analysis. Co-expression networks linking lncRNA-mRNA and circRNA-mRNA pairs, as well as ceRNA networks involving lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA and circRNA-miRNA-mRNA interactions, were constructed for differentially expressed (DE) RNAs. Key lncRNAs were validated by RT-qPCR. Transcriptional factor-lncRNA networks were constructed, and key relationships were verified using RIP-PCR. Results: Patients with HF-MI exhibited marked elevation of NT-proBNP and significant reduction in LVEF%. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed 228 DE-mRNAs, 700 DE-lncRNAs, and 1188 DE-circRNAs in HF-MI compared to non-heart failure patients (NHF-MI). Construction of the ceRNA network identified hsa-miR-6089 and hsa-miR-6771-5p as key miRNAs in the lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network, while hsa-miR-1207-5p and hsa-miR-10392-3p were key miRNAs in the circRNA-miRNA-mRNA network. PVT1, SNHG5, TTN-AS1, HCP5, and OIP5-AS1 were identified as the five key DE-lncRNAs, with PVT1/SNHG5 showing upregulation and TTN-AS1/HCP5/OIP5-AS1 exhibiting downregulation. The transcription factor-lncRNA network primarily involves GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1, with validated associative interactions. Conclusion: This study systematically mapped the regulatory network of HF-MI, revealing the roles of the GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1 regulatory axes in HF-MI, thereby providing a basis for exploring novel therapeutic strategies.

IntroductionPsychedelics and meditation are increasingly used for therapeutic and wellness purposes. However, research into adverse effects (AEs) has been limited, without adequate investigation of the nature, clinical characteristics, and diversity of persisting challenges following psychedelic use and meditation practice. This study aims to better characterize the clinical and contextual features of these challenges, describe their longitudinal course, and compare psychedelic-related challenges to meditation-related challenges, selected as comparator conditions given previously characterized phenomenological and contextual overlap between the two.

Methods and AnalysisThis is a mixed-methods, enriched-sample, active-comparator (psychedelics vs. meditation) observational study comprising (1) a cross-sectional retrospective survey (N = 1,600), (2) a prospective 12-month longitudinal design involving six bimonthly surveys (n = 800), (3) 12 weeks of weekly ambulatory assessments combining quantitative symptom ratings with narrative voice report (n = 40), and (4) qualitative interviews (n = 60). Participants are recruited into two parallel arms of 800 each: individuals reporting psychedelic-related challenges and individuals reporting meditation-related challenges, defined as distress or impairment persisting after the acute effects of a psychedelic experience or period of meditation practice have subsided. Data collection includes a tailored item pool aimed at capturing the symptoms and phenomenology of these challenges in detail, developed from qualitative research and collaboratively with stakeholders with lived experience. The World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0) and measures of agent/exposure, set, setting, and social response are administered to characterize biopsychosocial correlates and functional impacts of AEs. Initial analyses will describe the phenomenology, course, and functional impact of psychedelic- and meditation-related challenges, and evaluate the structure and psychometric properties of the novel item pool. The study will produce a publicly available de-identified dataset supporting subsequent analyses, such as correspondence with recognized clinical syndromes, trajectory characterization, and cross-arm comparison of measurement structure, reported in registered reports or preregistrations.
observations.title: Post-psychedelic and meditation-related challenges: a protocol for a mixed-methods longitudinal-observational study

observations.text: Accurate bacterial promoter prediction supports genome annotation, but many models use fixed-length promoter windows anchored to transcription start sites (TSSs) rather than promoter-element boundaries. We developed the General Bacterial Promoter Predictor (GBactPro), a convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) framework using promoter sequences resolved by the Promoter Architecture Scanner. Using Escherichia coli-trained models evaluated across 43 bacterial species, we compared eight input designs and identified the contiguous -35/spacer/-10 core as optimal (mean AUROC = 0.9859). Species-specific models showed broad transfer in a 43 x 43 evaluation. Joint training on all 43 species achieved a mean AUROC of 0.9943 across their held-out test sets and outperformed four established predictors under matched-length benchmarks. In genome-wide E. coli scanning, GBactPro achieved AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.979 and 0.160 under stringent full-containment matching (0-bp tolerance), increasing to 0.997 and 0.323 under a 100-bp tolerance. False-positive predictions overlapped H-NS binding regions more frequently than true positives (24.4% versus 18.8%), and predictions also overlapped promoters derepressed in an H-NS-knockout dataset. Prediction precision varied across four TSS classes. These findings demonstrate that element-resolved promoter definitions improve cross-species prediction and support genome-wide identification of candidate bacterial promoters.
observations.title: GBactPro: cross-species bacterial promoter prediction using element-resolved promoter definitions

BackgroundAccurate organ segmentation in pediatric focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST) is an important prerequisite for automated image analysis and image quality assessment, but manual segmentation is time-intensive, subject to inter- and intra-observer variability, and limits the scalability of deep learning dataset development. Although deep learning has shown promise for ultrasound organ segmentation, its application to pediatric FAST has not been evaluated.

ObjectiveTo describe the development and evaluation of deep learning models to automatically localize and segment six abdominal organs in pediatric FAST.

MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study using a convenience sample of archived FAST examinations from 200 injured children evaluated at a Level I pediatric trauma center. Emergency ultrasound fellowship-trained physicians manually segmented six key abdominal organs. Annotated image-mask pairs were split into training and test sets in an 80:20 ratio. We developed or fine-tuned U-Net, EVIT U-Net, UltraSAM, and nnU-Net models to automatically segment the bladder, kidney, liver, spleen, spine, and diaphragm. Segmentation accuracy was assessed using the Dice-Sorensen Coefficient (DSC) compared with manual annotations. Pediatric emergency ultrasound experts reviewed previously unlabeled FAST clips and rated the acceptability of model-generated organ masks.

ResultsThe dataset included 1,807 manually annotated image-mask pairs from 200 pediatric FAST clips. Using an 80:20 split with no overlap between video clips, 1,446 image-mask pairs were used for training and 361 for testing. Across all models and organs, mean DSC was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.84). Mean DSC was highest for the kidney and bladder, each 0.91 (95% CI: 0.87-0.95), and lowest for the diaphragm at 0.63 (95% CI: 0.60-0.67). EVIT U-Net achieved the highest DSC for kidney, liver, and spleen, performed comparably to the highest-performing models for bladder, and had a mean inference time of 54 milliseconds per image. In previously unlabeled pediatric FAST clips, experts rated model-generated organ masks as acceptable for localization in 73%-95% of clips across organs.

ConclusionWe describe the automatic segmentation of key abdominal organs in pediatric FAST with limited annotated data. This represents an important advancement in our image processing pipeline and can accelerate the development of large, robust datasets with segmentation for anatomy and pathology. Experts found that model-generated masks provided acceptable localization in most previously unlabeled pediatric clips, supporting the potential use of automated segmentation in pediatric FAST image analysis.
observations.title: Development and evaluation of automated organ segmentation models for abdominal ultrasound in injured children

metadata.summary: Cardiogenesis is a highly regulated developmental process that requires the coordinated occurrence of proliferation, differentiation, and contractility of cardiomyocytes, the specialized cardiac cells. However, the mechanisms that coordinate these processes remain incompletely understood.  Here, we demonstrate that cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of TRF2 in mice leads to severe cardiac malformations and results in embryonic lethality. Heterozygous TRF2 deletion is haploinsufficient, leading to progressive cardiac dysfunction, fibrosis, and early mortality. Despite unaltered telomere length, TRF2 loss impairs cardiomyocyte proliferation and induces DNA damage without activating apoptosis or p53-mediated rescue pathways. Mechanistically, TRF2 maintains heterochromatin organization by orchestrating cardiac gene activation programs. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized role for TRF2 in chromatin organization and cardiac development, offering new insights into the molecular underpinning of cardiac diseases.

observations.text: Cardiac damage in the aftermath of myocardial ischemia / reperfusion (MI/R) compromises both electrical and mechanical function, predisposing patients to arrhythmia and heart failure. Microvascular obstruction (MVO) is increasingly recognized as a sequela of MI/R and a contributor to proarrhythmic cardiac remodeling. While transvalvular unloading (TVU) using a percutaneously delivered pump is garnering appreciation as a means of limiting infarct size and preserving mechanical function following percutaneous coronary intervention, its benefits for arrhythmia prevention remain unclear. We used a porcine model to test the hypothesis that cardiac unloading prior to and through reperfusion mitigates MVO, preserves cardiomyocyte nanostructure, and alleviates arrhythmias following MI/R. Anesthetized domestic swine undergoing acute ischemia (LAD occlusion, 90 mins) and reperfusion (120 mins) were randomized to TVU (n=5) and no treatment (control; n=6) treatments. Thioflavin-S was infused into the mid-LAD to assess coronary microcirculation and quantify MVO. Arrhythmia burden was assessed by in vivo electrocardiography using 3 lead EKG. Cardiac tissues were preserved for histology and optical microscopy studies. Compared to no treatment controls, TVU hearts evidenced significantly reduced infarct area (48 +/- 5 % vs. 59 +/- 11 % p = 0.03) and MVO (19 +/- 4 % vs. 27 +/- 5% , p = 0.03) normalized to area at risk and a higher myocardial salvage index (52 +/- 5 % vs. 41 +/- 11% p = 0.03). Extensive perivascular edema, and neutrophil infiltration observed in controls was markedly reduced in TVU hearts. Confocal microscopy and spatial pattern analysis revealed significantly mitigated disruption of gap junctions and NaV1.5 dissociation from N-cadherin in TVU hearts compared to controls. Importantly, severity-adjusted arrhythmia burden during reperfusion was significantly lower in TV-P hearts (8+/-8 vs. 12+/-5 episodes lasting greater than 5seconds in controls). Our results demonstrate that TVU effectively prevents arrhythmias during reperfusion by preserving coronary microvasculature and cardiomyocyte nanostructure.
observations.title: Cardiac unloading via a transvalvular pump prevents arrhythmias following myocardial ischemia / reperfusion by preserving coronary microcirculation and cardiomyocyte nanostructure

observations.text: Background: Schizophrenia is a severe neuropsychiatric disorder. Efforts to describe the underlying biology and establish diagnostic markers through non-invasive neuroimaging methods are ongoing, resulting in a range of theoretical brain-based frameworks. Prominent frameworks for aberrant schizophrenia-associated functional connectivity in resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rsfMRI) include the dysconnectivity hypothesis, theory of cognitive dysmetria, and triple network theory. Although informative, prior work can be improved by increasing sample size, avoiding confirmation bias, and accounting for individual variability and the effects of medication and chronicity. Methods: With these recommendations in mind, we employed a data-driven, whole-brain approach using a large multi-site rsfMRI dataset (N = 2,656; schizophrenia = 1,248). We used reference-guided independent component analysis to generate subject-specific whole-brain functional network connectivity (FNC) and extract imaging markers of similarity to schizophrenia patterns. We modeled the relationship between medication dosage, age of onset, chronicity, symptom severity, and cognitive performance and FNC. Results: Our analysis identified a reliable schizophrenia-FNC signature characterized by aberrantly stronger negative cerebellothalamic and positive thalamocortical connectivity, implicating sensory, motor, and associative cortical circuits. While medication and chronicity were significantly associated with these signatures, the core cerebellothalamic disruptions remained a robust marker of schizophrenia. Conclusions: This work represents the largest schizophrenia-specific rsfMRI study to date, refines existing theoretical frameworks with a more nuanced map of how clinical variables interact with brain connectivity, and provides a high-fidelity template of schizophrenia-related connectivity. We have released this template as an open-access resource to facilitate reproducibility and accelerate the development of reliable rsfMRI-based schizophrenia biomarkers.
observations.title: NeuroMark-SZ: A Holistic Resting-State-fMRI-Based Model for Divergent Functional Circuitry in Schizophrenia

observations.text: Complete connectomes now exist for insect nervous systems, but whether a fixed wiring diagram can learn, and what its memories consist of, is unknown. Here, we trained a spiking model of the whole male Drosophila central nervous system, 167,106 neurons with fixed wiring, to plan moves and to remember a visual cue. Spikes write the cue into neuronal adaptation, which holds it silently until the next input reads it out. Cells that hold the trace are enriched for transcripts of a calcium-activated potassium channel in fly cell atlases. The learned readout recalls the trace only in the brain state of learning: the same trace evokes a different response at another delay, and a disease-like loss of potassium current rewrites the trace and changes how it is read. Learning in the new state is spared. Memory failure can arise from a change of state rather than a loss of storage.

metadata.summary: Obesity-induced metabolic cardiomyopathy features myocardial lipid overload, mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation, with few targeted therapies. Hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA), a natural secondary bile acid, plays key roles in metabolic homeostasis, yet its direct cardioprotective effects in obesity-related cardiac injury remain unclear. Here, we investigated HDCA effects on high-fat diet-induced cardiomyopathy using in vivo, lipotoxic cardiomyocyte and 3D cardiac spheroid models. HDCA ameliorated cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophic remodeling and myocardial lipid accumulation. Transcriptomics showed HDCA remodelled cardiac programs governing mitochondrial and lipid metabolism as well as inflammation. Mechanistically, HDCA limited cardiomyocyte lipid uptake via TGR5-dependent suppression of CD36 membrane localization, boosted mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, and reduced oxidative stress. HDCA also bound PIK3CA to inhibit PI3K-AKT-mediated inflammation. In 3D cardiac spheroids, HDCA alleviated lipotoxic injury. Collectively, HDCA protects against obesity-associated cardiomyopathy by coordinating myocardial lipid metabolism, mitochondrial homeostasis and inflammatory signaling, representing a promising candidate for metabolic heart disease.

observations.title: Hyodeoxycholic acid protects against obesity-associated cardiomyopathy by restoring myocardial metabolic homeostasis and suppressing inflammatory remodeling

observations.text: Reliable clinical translation of diagnostic artificial intelligence (AI) requires evaluation beyond classification accuracy. We developed PedDx, a segmentation-free framework for pediatric posterior fossa tumor diagnosis using T2-weighted MRI, pretrained 3DINO representations, calibrated predictions, and confidence-based abstention. Evaluation included 492 discovery, 114 replication, 129 external validation, and 40 independently tested cases, alongside 236 out-of-distribution (OOD) cases and controlled imaging perturbations. Classification accuracy was 79.8% in replication and 81.4% in external validation, increasing to 90.5% and 88.7%, respectively, among non-abstained cases. OOD analyses revealed performance degradation and confidently incorrect predictions, while perturbation analyses identified acquisition and alignment vulnerabilities. An external institution independently executed the complete agentic workflow, successfully generating predictions and structured quality-control reports for all 40 cases, with classification accuracy of 92.5%, increasing to 97.3% among non-abstained cases. PedDx demonstrates how uncertainty assessment, failure-mode characterization, external validation, and independently reproducible, traceable reporting can collectively inform the reliability and limitations of diagnostic AI systems.
observations.title: PedDx: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis with Agentic AI-Enabled Independent External Evaluation

metadata.summary: Laminopathies comprise a diverse array of phenotypes that involve multiple organs and are caused by mutations in the LMNA gene, which encodes nuclear envelope protein lamin A (LMNA). Cardiac involvement is a prominent feature and a major cause of mortality and morbidity in laminopathies. LMNA interacts with chromatin through lamin-associated domains (LADs) and regulates gene expression. The role of the LMNA in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression in cardiac myocytes is unknown.  We conditionally deleted the Lmna gene specifically in cardiac myocytes in the mouse, isolated the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes, and characterized genomic structure and function at two levels: first, by identifying and characterizing the genome-wide CTCF binding sites by a CUT&RUN assay; and second, the chromatin conformational changes by HiC.  To determine the role of LMNA in genome organization and gene expression we integrated CTCF binding, LAD, Hi-C data with the gene expression (RNA-seq), and DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs), determined by END-Seq, in cardiac myocytes.  Compared to wild-type (WT) myocytes, LMNA deficiency increased genomic occupancy of CTCF , predominantly outside of the constitutive LADs (cLADs), and increased gene expression at the CTCF binding sites. Likewise, DSBs were highly enriched at the CTCF binding sites. However, only a small fraction of the chromatin compartments was shifted in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. LMNA-deficiency changed the organization of one-third of the topologically-associated domains (TADs). The changes were characterized by the merger of 2 or more TADs (60%), mainly in the non-LAD regions, splitting (30%), and shifting boundaries (10%). Reorganization of TADs, however, did not directly affect gene expression or the prevalence of DSBs. A remarkable effect of the LMNA deficiency was on chromatin loops, as it led to a gain of ~ 600 and a loss of ~1000 loops, whose boundaries were enriched in the CTCF binding sites. The changes affected the transcript level of ~25% of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. The gain of the loop was associated with increased gene expression, whereas the loss of the loop had the opposite effect. A multivariate analysis showed that differential CTCF  binding  (largest), loops, and cLADs affected the transcript levels of the DEGs, whereas TADs and chromatin compartments appeared to act in concert with these factors  rather than as independent determinants.  In conclusion, LMNA regulates chromatin structure like TADs its role in  gene expression is mediated mainly through CTCF, cLADs, and loops,. The findings provide insights into the molecular pathogenesis of cardiac involvement in the diverse array of phenotypes in laminopathies.

observations.title: Effects of the Lamin A on Chromatin Structure and Function in Cardiac Myocytes in a Mouse Model of Lamin-Cardiomyopathy

BackgroundMRI-visible perivascular spaces (PVS) are an imaging marker of compromised brain health function. However, robust PVS segmentation remains challenging: conventional methods often require cohort-specific parameter tuning, while supervised deep-learning models depend on extensive manual annotations for training and may fail to generalise to unseen scanners, protocols, and clinical populations.

MethodsWe introduce DRIPS (Domain Randomisation for Image-based PVS Segmentation), a fully automated deep-learning framework trained exclusively on synthetic data. By learning PVS representations from a plethora of simulated cases, DRIPS transfers to real-world MRI without using manually labelled PVS data from real participants. We evaluated DRIPS in 185 fully manually annotated MRI scans from eight independent cohorts encompassing diverse clinical populations and acquisition settings, including 3T and 7T imaging, T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, and isotropic and anisotropic resolutions. DRIPS was compared with five previously published methods.

ResultsAcross cohorts, DRIPS significantly outperformed the second-best method for both area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) and centreline Dice similarity coefficient (clDice), with mean gains of at least 0.1: 0.146 for basal ganglia (BG) AUPRC (P = 0.008), 0.125 for centrum semiovale (CSO) AUPRC (P = 0.008), 0.112 for BG clDice (P = 0.016), and 0.186 for CSO clDice (P = 0.008). Importantly, its performance was not associated with white matter hyperintensity burden.

ConclusionsDRIPS enables accurate, fully automated PVS segmentation across heterogeneous imaging settings without the need for real PVS annotations for training.
observations.title: DRIPS: Domain Randomisation for Image-based Perivascular spaces Segmentation

metadata.summary: Multiplex assays of variant effects have linked thousands of genotypes to fitness effects, yet we lack profound understanding of how variants impact molecular phenotypes. Here, we introduce a deep mutational scanning framework that quantifies disease-determining molecular phenotypes in human cells, allowing readouts of protein localization and splicing regulatory function at scale. Applied to the dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)-associated protein RBM20, we profiled ~4,300 amino acid substitutions across disease-linked protein domains. We discovered new variant hotspots affecting protein functions, complemented by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure-function investigations of RBM20 bound to its nuclear import receptor TNPO3. Finally, we systematically probed nuclear relocalization to identify variants that retain overall splicing ability and therefore may be amenable to this therapeutic strategy. Together, we created comprehensive variant-to-function maps that predict variant impact, enhance clinical interpretation, and stratify RBM20-mediated DCM into mechanistically distinct therapeutic classes.

metadata.summary: Background: Reactive oxygen species are increased across most pulmonary hypertension (PH) etiologies, resulting in increased reactive lipid dicarbonyls, which form protein adducts and impair mitochondrial function. We hypothesized that reducing reactive lipids would reduce right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) and improve cardiac function by eliminating protein-lipid damage feedback loops. Methods: We used 2-hydroxybenzylamine (2-HOBA) to scavenge reactive lipids in three complimentary mouse models of PH: AKR-high fat diet (HFD, metabolic stress), LNAME-HFD (cardiometabolic syndrome), and pulmonary artery banding (PAB, load stress). Cardiac function was measured by echocardiography and catheterization. RV energy metabolism was determined by oxygraphy. Mass spectrometry analyzed lipids and ceramides; O-link and RNA-Seq evaluated proteomic and gene expression in lungs, RV, and LV. Results: Reducing reactive lipids with 2-HOBA resulted in a ~10% reduction in RVSP, reduced diastolic dysfunction, reduced plasma lipids and ceramides, and normalized RV fatty acid oxidation that was severely impaired in the AKR-HFD and PAB models. Proteomic and RNA changes in the lungs, RV, and LV suggested reduced oxidative damage and inflammatory signaling and altered developmental and actin organization signaling; these changes are plausibly associated with the improved adaptation. Some changes were sex specific, including a 4x higher cardiac fatty acid content in males than females. Conclusions: Reactive lipid scavenging improves cardiac metabolic and diastolic function and pulmonary vascular resistance through restoration of mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative protein damage. The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

observations.title: Reducing Reactive Lipids Improves Cardiac Metabolic and Diastolic Function in Pulmonary Hypertension Models

metadata.summary: Background. Rheumatic heart valve disease (RHVD) is the leading cause of acquired valvular disease worldwide, driven by autoimmune responses that sustain chronic inflammation and fibrotic remodeling, predominantly affecting the mitral valve (MV). Although immune dysregulation and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling are implicated, the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression and their relationship to clinical severity remain incompletely defined. Methods. We performed a tissue-centric multi-omics study combining histopathology, unbiased proteomics of human MV tissue (n=72), and plasma proteomics from an external cohort (n=445). We associated proteomic signatures with clinical parameters. Cross-species validation involved single-cell RNA sequencing from a murine model of autoimmune valvular carditis. Mechanistic studies used primary human valvular interstitial cells (VICs) and a three-dimensional MV mimetics. Results. RHVD MVs exhibited leaflet thickening, fibrosis, immune cell infiltration, and neovascularization, with T-cell abundance correlating with tissue remodeling. Proteomic profiling identified 1,436 differentially expressed proteins enriched in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, immune response, hemostasis, and multi-growth factor signaling, including TGF-β and insulin-like growth factor binding protein (IGFBP) pathway. Integrated tissue-plasma analysis revealed shared molecular signatures. The mean transvalvular gradient captured the hemodynamic continuum from mitral regurgitation to stenosis and was associated with coordinated with ECM remodeling, cytoskeletal, immune, and hemostatic pathways. Cross-species integration confirmed convergence on ECM remodeling, immune activation, and TGF-β/IGFBP signaling, predominantly in VIC and myofibroblast populations. Mechanistically, TGF-β induced IGFBP5, IGFBP7, and CCN2 expression in VICs, while their silencing attenuated collagen expression. MV mimetics exposed to pro-fibrotic and inflammatory stimuli recapitulated these findings. Conclusions. TGF-β-centered signaling networks drive the coordinated immune, and fibrotic remodeling that characterizes RHVD. The TGF-β-IGFBP axis emerges as a key mediator of VIC-driven fibrosis and links molecular remodeling to clinical disease progression, highlighting novel therapeutic opportunities.

metadata.summary: Reperfusion of ischemic myocardium triggers a sterile inflammatory cascade in which NF-κB–dependent transcriptional priming precedes NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and caspase-1 activation. Diacerein, approved for osteoarthritis, is converted in vivo to rhein, an NF-κB inhibitor with inflammasome-attenuating properties, but its effect on the ischemic myocardial transcriptome is unknown.  To define the transcriptional program underlying diacerein-mediated cardioprotection, male Wistar rats received oral diacerein (80 mg/kg/day) or vehicle for 10 days before the heart was isolated and subjected to global no-flow ischemia followed by reperfusion in a Langendorff preparation. RNA sequencing of left ventricular tissue identified 314 differentially expressed genes (268 downregulated, 46 upregulated) in diacerein- versus vehicle-treated hearts. Downregulated genes included Selp (P-selectin), the endothelial adhesion molecule mediating leukocyte capture, Csf2rb (the shared GM-CSF/IL-3/IL-5 receptor subunit), and Ripk1, while Card9 was upregulated. Gene set enrichment analysis showed suppression of TNF signaling, NF-κB signaling, and cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction pathways.  These data indicate that diacerein pretreatment suppresses leukocyte recruitment and inflammatory priming programs in the ischemic myocardium, and provide a transcriptional basis for its cardioprotective effect.

metadata.summary: Environmental exposures to toxic chemicals can profoundly alter the transcriptome and epigenome in both humans and animals, contributing to disease development across the lifespan. To elucidate how early-life exposure to toxicants exerts such persistent effects, the Toxicant Exposures and Responses by Genomic and Epigenomic Regulators of Transcription II (TaRGET II) Consortium generated a landmark resource comprising 2,570 epigenomes and 1,043 transcriptomes from longitudinal studies in mice. All data are publicly available through the TaRGET II data portal and the WashU Epigenome Browser. This resource from target (liver, brain, lung, heart) and surrogate (blood) tissues at weaning (3 weeks) and two adult time-points (5 and 10 months) characterized the molecular response to arsenic (As), lead (Pb), bisphenol-A (BPA), di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate(DEHP), tributyltin (TBT), tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD), and particulate matter with a diameter of <2.5μm (PM2.5). The findings revealed persistent, toxicant-specific, sex-dependent epigenomic and transcriptomic perturbations, resulting in disrupted expression of 14,908 genes, altered chromatin accessibility at 87,409 regulatory elements, DNA methylation changes at 113,186 genomic regions, and chromatin state switching of histone modifications. The resulting high-resolution map of how environmental exposures reprogram the epigenome and transcriptome is broadly accessible via ToxiTaRGET database, offering unparalleled opportunities for the scientific community to investigate the molecular underpinnings of environmental toxicant exposures and their contributions to disease pathogenesis.

observations.text: Latent inhibition (LI) refers to the reduced ability to learn or express learning about a stimulus following prior exposure to it without consequence. It has been extensively studied to investigate associative learning and memory as well as the aberrant attribution of salience to irrelevant stimuli in both humans and animals, a process which is thought to underpin hallucinations and delusions in psychosis. Despite sex differences observed in numerous aspects of psychosis, few studies have attempted to characterise sex differences in LI. This systematic review outlines the current evidence of sex differences in LI in both human and rodent studies, showing predominantly inconclusive and conflicting evidence for sex differences. However, the majority of cases in which sex differences were found were in studies that assessed the impact of additional factors on LI such as drug administration, juvenile handling, and oestrous phase, and demonstrated interactions between sex and these additional factors. Hence, there is stronger evidence for sex differences in vulnerability to perturbations in LI. Furthermore, we present data demonstrating sex differences in latent inhibition of contextual fear conditioning and associated gene expression in the hippocampus in rodents, suggesting sex differences in hippocampal processing underpinning latent inhibition at both the behavioural and neurobiological levels. Although there have been relatively few studies demonstrating sex differences in LI identified by the systematic review, the data suggest that in hippocampally dependent forms of LI, sex differences may be more apparent, which may be of relevance in relation to sex differences in the presentation of psychosis.
observations.title: Sex differences in latent inhibition and their implications for psychotic disorders

Background and ObjectivesAmyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease primarily affecting motor neurons but also frequently involving cognitive impairment. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) measurements of {beta}-amyloid peptides (A{beta}40, A{beta}42), tau proteins, and neurofilaments are clinically established biomarkers in Alzheimers disease (AD). Emerging evidence suggests that AD-related pathological changes and AD-related biomarkers may appear in ALS, yet their diagnostic and prognostic significance remains incompletely understood.

MethodsIn this retrospective study, we analyzed clinical and CSF biomarker data from patients with ALS, AD, Huntingtons disease (HD), and other disease controls from real-world clinical settings. The dataset comprised A{beta}40, A{beta}42, total tau (t-Tau), phosphorylated tau181 (pTau181), phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNfH), and relevant serum markers as well as clinical and cognitive status measurements. Additionally, longitudinal CSF sampling over one year was evaluated in three ALS patients receiving tofersen treatment.

ResultsIn this real-world cohort, AD-related CSF biomarkers demonstrated no diagnostic value for distinguishing ALS from other neurodegenerative conditions. However, A{beta}40, A{beta}42, and pTau181 levels correlated positively with ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) global score and serum Creatine Kinase MB (CK-MB) concentrations. At the same time, a higher A{beta}42/A{beta}40 ratio was associated with better memory performance on the Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen (ECAS). In tofersen-treated cases, AD-related biomarkers gradually declined during follow-up.

DiscussionThese findings suggest that elevated CSF AD-associated biomarkers in ALS may reflect preserved functional and cognitive status and exhibited parallel declines during follow-up in three tofersen-treated patients, supporting their further prospective evaluation as exploratory markers of therapeutic responsiveness.

observations.text: Reward-related changes in hippocampal place-cell activity may reflect either different use of an existing spatial map or plasticity that reshapes the map. We separated these contributions in a two-pathway model: a recurrent network learned to predict sensory input and developed a spatial representation, while a reinforcement-learning controller combined this representation with an explicit goal signal to guide behavior. Replaying identical trajectories before and after learning isolated representational plasticity. Goal-directed behavior strongly concentrated place fields near reward, whereas changes to the representation were smaller and more variable. A reward-proximity teaching signal made these changes larger and more consistent, and the change was strongly attenuated when recurrent plasticity was restricted. After reward relocation, goal-related directional tuning adapted more fully than place-field organization, while withdrawing reward and proximity teaching reversed the learned field concentration. Thus, reward affects predictive spatial maps through separable mechanisms: goal information changes how an existing map is used, whereas reward-related teaching signals reshape the map itself. Our results provide a concrete framework for future experiments to disentangle how reward information, plasticity and behavior jointly shape hippocampal activity.
observations.title: Reward changes the use and structure of predictive spatial maps

Background and AimsArtificial intelligence (AI) may help differentiate Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) on electrocardiograms (ECGs). We developed an ECG image-based model and evaluated whether AI assistance and visual explanations improved reader performance, overall and by reader background.

MethodsA self-supervised three-architecture deep learning ensemble was developed and externally validated using 12-lead ECG images from two institutions, recorded [≤]14 days after onset regardless of reperfusion. A four-phase reader study compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and AI assistance (Phases 1-3). In Phase 4, readers were randomized to the reference sheet alone, AI predictions, or predictions with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Correctness was analyzed with generalized linear mixed-effects models.

ResultsCohorts comprised 832 development and 95 external validation participants. External validation accuracy was 0.914, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.970 (95% CI, 0.938-0.992), or 0.958 using first recorded ECGs. Among 70 readers, the estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 unaided to 0.864 with AI (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference sheet (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95), and Grad-CAM added value (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25). In exploratory analyses, less experienced readers gained more; with AI, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. Mean AI-assisted reader accuracy remained below model accuracy.

ConclusionsAn ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader performance, particularly with visual explanations. Experience-related differences emphasize the need for effective human-AI interaction.

metadata.summary: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked fatal disorder caused by dystrophin deficiency, characterized by early-onset, progressive degeneration of skeletal and cardiac muscle. Although microdystrophin (µDys) gene therapies provide functional benefit and partially restore tissue architecture, their impact on disease-associated cellular programs remains unclear. We evaluated proprietary codon-optimized µDys delivered via AAV8 under the MHCK7 promoter and a MyoD enhancer in severe DMD rats with an exon 52 deletion (DMDdel52). Therapy achieved sustained µDys expression with 90-97% of myofibers and cardiomyocytes, with proteins levels ranging from physiological to supra-physiological. Treatment preserved muscle function and extended survival beyond the median lifespan of untreated DMDdel52 rats, maintaining ambulation, climbing, weight gain, and muscle strength. Treatment also preserved cardiac architecture and function while preventing myonecrosis and adverse remodeling, with no detectable toxicity despite high µDys expression. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that µDys treatment prevented disease-associated inflammatory and fibrotic activation of fibro-adipogenic progenitors, preserved a pro-regenerative interstitial environment and muscle stem cell quiescence while preventing senescence marker expression. These findings indicate that early µDys gene therapy preserves muscle homeostasis, function, and lifespan by preventing disease-associated cellular programs from becoming established within the regenerative niche of DMD rats.

To test the hypothesis that SVs from people with congenital heart disease (CHD) patients disrupt developmental chromatin interactions, we developed CardioAkita, a machine-learning model that predicts how variants alter 3D chromatin structure. Analyzing previously genotyped de novo SVs (dnSVs), we observed positive associations between CHD severity and CardioAkita scores across dozens of families. Induced pluripotent stem cells engineered to harbor these variants confirmed CardioAkita’s predictions of disrupted 3D chromatin organization, and further revealed aberrant expression of local genes including cardiac developmental genes, suggesting that chromatin reorganization plays a significant mechanistic role in the genetic etiology of CHD. Our findings highlight the potential for predictive models of 3D chromatin organization thus have potential to predict the pathogenicity and underlying mechanisms of SVs in human disease.

metadata.summary: INTRODUCTION: Adipose tissue plays a significant role in metabolism with cross-organ communication through adipokines and hormones. Sex-hormones have a special influence over the distribution and function of adipose tissue which varies based on gender. Gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) is prescribed widely among transgender patients but its long-term effect on metabolism is still unclear. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we investigated the longitudinal effects of GAHT of uniform regimen among 24 hormone-naïve individuals on adipose tissue metabolism, body composition, and insulin sensitivity. Patients with diabetes and certain comorbidities or taking medications affecting glucose metabolism were excluded. Baseline and follow up assessments at 6 months and 12 months included clinical parameters such as blood pressure, weight, BMI and waist and hip circumference measurements, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) for body composition, fasting blood samples for sex hormone levels, metabolic and inflammatory markers, and abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies for histological and transcriptomic analyses. RESULTS: After one year of GAHT, transfemales showed expected changes in sex hormone level along with increase in body fat (MD - 4.4, p= 0.17); metabolic changes such as increased cardiac markers NT-proBNP (MD -18.04, p = 0.002), Galectin-3 (MD -10567.4, p = 9.41E-05) and decrease in alkaline phosphatase (MD 15.13, p = 0.0006), and certain ceramides such as lactosyl C24 (MD 193439.9, p = 0.03) and sphingosine- 1-phosphate (MD 533175.7, p = 0.04). In transmales, testosterone therapy led to reduced fat mass [total body fat (MD 5.01, P-value 0.02) and limb fat (MD 3183.18, p = 0.04)]; increased lean mass (MD -2184. 19, p = 0.50) with improvements in insulin sensitivity [HOMA-IR (MD 0.64, p = 0.05) and ADIPO-IR (MD 2.54, p = 0.01)] and adipose tissue metabolism evidenced by reduced fat cell size and favorable adipokine profile. RNA sequencing of adipose tissue revealed altered gene expression patterns with a shift toward reduced inflammation and improved metabolic function among transmales. CONCLUSION: These findings confirm some of the known effect of GAHT in previous studies while providing additional mechanistic insights into distinct metabolic and adipose tissue changes among transgender individuals; with transmales experiencing improved insulin sensitivity and favorable adipose tissue remodeling. This is the first study known to us with comprehensive and longitudinal data on metabolic impact of GAHT, emphasizing the need for individualized monitoring and risk management of underlying chronic disease among transgender population taking GAHT.

metadata.summary: Muscle LIM Protein (MLP) is a key component of the cardiomyocyte Z disc that is essential for sarcomere integrity and cardiac homeostasis.  Loss of MLP function results in (cardio)myopathy phenotypes in animal models and is associated with inherited cardiomyopathies in humans. Here, we identify MLP as an evolutionarily conserved non-canonical RNA-binding protein and uncover RNA binding as a previously unrecognized mechanism involved in its cytoskeletal association. Using enhanced RNA interactome capture together with complementary biochemical approaches, we demonstrate direct RNA binding by MLP and map two short RNA-binding motifs adjacent to its LIM domains. Disrupting these motifs markedly reduces RNA association, including residues associated with cardiomyopathies. Mechanistically, RNA is required for MLP’s interactions with cytoskeletal proteins, and for the formation of higher-order MLP-containing assemblies. Consistently, RNA-binding-deficient MLP mutants exhibit impaired interactions with cytoskeletal proteins and reduced cytoskeletal retention. Our findings reveal the importance of RNA binding for the formation of MLP assemblies, and support the emerging role of RNA as a co-factor in the organization of macromolecular complexes, with potential relevance to human disease.

BackgroundChange in cognitive control is a candidate transdiagnostic mechanism of psychedelic therapy. One account predicts that, once acute effects resolve, psilocybin shifts control toward flexibility while sparing inhibition and working memory. A motivational account (PRISM) predicts that psilocybin increases the willingness to exert control rather than the ability to do so. We tested both in patients with co-occurring alcohol use disorder (AUD) and major depression.

MethodsIn this secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of psilocybin for AUD with comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04620759), a subset of participants (placebo n=13, psilocybin n=12) completed five cognitive tasks before drug administration and again about one week after it (mean 6.7 days, SD 1.1). Outcome measures spanned the stability-flexibility continuum. Free choice between levels of cognitive demand indexed the participants willingness to exert control. Effect sizes and Bayes factors were used to estimate drug effects and associations with change in drinking and depressive symptoms across 34 retest measures.

ResultsRelative to placebo, psilocybin slowed responding in cued task switching (learning-phase RT d=1.01, BF10=7.7; switch trials d=1.12, BF10=17). Psilocybin effects on feedback-driven measures were inconsistent in direction (7 of 11 toward flexibility); the largest was on perseveration, which rose less with practice under psilocybin than under placebo (d=-0.79, BF10=1.1). Other drug effects on the 34 retest measures had inconclusive Bayes factors (BF10=0.40-2.4), and none survived false discovery rate correction. Demand avoidance, analyzed separately from the 34 measures, showed no detectable drug effect (BF01=2.0). Baseline demand avoidance showed no detectable relation to performance but tracked depressive symptoms (rs=.71, BF10=24). Drinking fell in both arms, and on 15 of 17 stability-flexibility measures change toward stability accompanied drinking reduction (stability composite rs=-.64, BF10=29; rs=-.43 when change was adjusted for baseline scores). Lower baseline working-memory span predicted larger drinking reductions (BF10=19-25). Depressive symptoms fell more after psilocybin than after placebo (PHQ-9, d=-0.88, BF10=2.7), but their change was not associated with cognitive change or predicted by working-memory span.

ConclusionsAbout one week after dosing, psilocybin slowed cued task switching but had no consistent effect on feedback-driven flexibility, and there was no evidence of an effect on the willingness to exert effort. Drinking reduction was associated with increased, not reduced, cognitive stability, whereas improvement in depressive symptoms was not associated with cognitive change. These pilot estimates can guide adequately powered trials.
